891354fdf71c1ff1b9f5258c0ee3fc46575bf7f5.summary: Genians Security Center (GSC) describes a reply-based spearphishing campaign that impersonated a senior aide in a South Korean National Assembly member's office in September 2026. The LNK-based chain used PowerShell and a public note page as a command channel, and the operator swapped in XenoRAT, information-collection and document-theft scripts, then NodeLinkRAT, a Node.js-based remote access tool, on October 16, 2026. GSC assesses the campaign as Kimsuky with moderate confidence.

actors.q: GSC therefore assesses this campaign as the work of the North Korea-linked threat group Kimsuky, with moderate confidence.

hedges: GSC assesses the Kimsuky attribution with moderate confidence; no single decisive piece of evidence has been obtained.
Attribution from individual factors alone is difficult, since XenoRAT and Dropbox or free hosting are widely abused by many actors.
Third-party imitation of the same techniques cannot be completely ruled out.
Deliberate deception is possible, since Korean strings and South Korean services may reflect targeting or be used to mislead.
Some attack stages may not have been identified, because the note page code changed frequently.
Victim-specific code selection through another, unconfirmed method cannot be ruled out.
Organisational changes in North Korean actors may cause partial overlap or confusion with their previous campaigns.
